body:
### Summary

With a cooldown configured via `exclude-newer`, `uv tree --outdated` reports as "latest" the newest version that is *installable* under the cooldown config. However, it gives no indication when an even newer release exists that is still inside the cooldown window. 

That signal is exactly what I need to decide whether to bump now or wait a few days. The point of a cooldown is to avoid adopting a release right after it ships, so if a newer release is already out I would rather wait for it to clear
the cooldown than upgrade twice. Today the only way to find out is to run the command a second time with `--exclude-newer false` and diff the two outputs.

I would like `--outdated` to mark packages where `exclude-newer` hid one or more newer releases, for example by appending the newest excluded version and when its installable.

Related: #18819, #18899, #19864 (a commenter there suggests a "newer version was ignored because of exclude-newer" warning during resolution, which is the same signal at a different point).

### Example

With the following cooldown in `pyproject.toml`

```toml
[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "7 days"
```

We are getting the following output today

```console
$ uv tree --outdated --depth=1
├── ruff v0.16.5 (group: dev) (latest: v0.17.2)

$ uv tree --outdated --depth=1 --exclude-newer false
├── ruff v0.16.5 (group: dev) (latest: v0.17.3)
```

Proposed output:

```console
$ uv tree --outdated --depth=1
├── ruff v0.16.5 (group: dev) (latest: v0.17.2, v0.17.3 installable after 2026-11-03T00:33:29)
```
title: tree --outdated should indicate when a newer version exists but is excluded by exclude-newer
